pr8.title: feat(codex): expose native account login for existing frontend workflows
pr8.body:
## Why
The existing frontend offers browser and device-code Codex login. The extracted app-server client currently exposes account reads/refresh/logout but cannot drive those login workflows through Host custody.

## Changes
Add finite typed account/login/start, account/login/cancel and private completion observation. Preserve native login IDs, unknown acceptance and no replay. The consumer keeps browser presentation, early-ID correlation, process custody, credential ownership and account readback. Session SPI and conversation event delivery remain compatible.

## Validation
Node 24.21.0 / pnpm 11.18.0: pnpm check passed (build, typecheck, 509 source tests and both packed consumers). The subprocess protocol suite covers 7 login cases. Node 26.11.1 / pnpm 11.18.0 also passed the complete check (509 source tests and both packed consumers). The retained packed-consumer artifact has SHA-256 `691a7a62cdd5a92e2edb120f2c409790c9ca16215495cdf9daa099b3b8748bd9`; the Session SPI archive is byte-identical to the frontend's current pin. This is protocol evidence, not vendor authentication or Desktop UI acceptance.

Frontend integration: https://github.com/777genius/agent-teams-ai/pull/1186
Plan: docs/plans/provider-migration/frontend-parity-2026-11-12/01-codex-login.md in that repository.

No package/release publication or default-branch merge.

pr10.title: fix: fence stale Claude suggestions and uncertain Codex samples
pr10.body: ## Problem Two opt-in prompt-suggestion paths can lose the identity or cancellation ownership of their original native work. Claude can restore A's suggestion slot after B was already accepted, and its wire event cannot identify a late A frame after B completes. Codex drops the sent sample's cancellation handle when its local RPC timeout expires, allowing later auxiliary work while the original sample remains unknown. ## Scope and current stage This isolated repair branch preserves all 43 commits and both Thinking changes through `9423f600dfb04d04448326dbced89919924b0b5f`. It does not move PR #8's shared head. The published R1 is §14 of `docs/plans/2026-11-14-native-next-prompt-suggestions.md`, commit `3ac086d1c157645faa358f0578f8dc764c950d66`. The current stage contains documentation only. Two additive finite-fixture test files come next. Both actual semantic REDs and independent source review are required before the bounded Claude Session and Codex app-server producer changes. The intended behavior is auxiliary-only lifetime quarantine for ambiguous Claude attribution and an unknown-sample latch plus at-most-once cancellation of Codex's original sent request. Ordinary inputs, readiness, queueing, deadlines, interactions and physical cleanup remain under their existing contracts. Suggestions remain default-off. ## Validation and boundaries Use the unchanged original `pnpm check` CI on Node 24.21.0 and 26.11.1 with pnpm 11.18.0, including both packed consumers. Earlier 9423 results—540 controlled passes and its checked archive pair—remain historical evidence and do not qualify the repair. Retain exact-head RED/GREEN logs and the newly checked archive pair before any separate atomic consumer adoption. Keep this PR Draft. The four original workflows were reviewed: safe CI is reachable; the Codex native job is Draft-skipped; Claude native and native OpenCode V2 paths do not match this bounded repair. No real Claude/Codex executable, SDK process, model request or version command; no manual dispatch, rerun, cancellation, native qualification or deadline extension. Product composer work and application archive/SPI adoption are outside this PR. --- ## Summary by cubic Fences stale Claude suggestions and uncertain Codex samples in the optional prompt-suggestion paths. Claude accepted-queue ordering can let a delayed earlier suggestion restore its slot after a successor was admitted, and the wire event has no input ID to disambiguate it. Codex local RPC expiry discards the only cancellation handle for a potentially sent sample, leaving unknown auxiliary work. - Claude: tracks the original suggestion owner; successor admission, interrupt, or uncertainty latches auxiliary offers off for the Query's lifetime, with no invented recovery criterion. - Codex: retains the sent sample's ID, latches auxiliary sampling on uncertain settlement, and attempts at most one targeted `thread/sample/cancel` while the transport is open. - Adds regression fixtures to `claude-sdk.test.ts` and `codex-subprocess.test.ts` plus the R1 plan documenting the defects and edit boundary. Suggestions remain default-off; no real Claude/Codex process is invoked. Written for commit c79b81bf002eaac95436da71c7049d7f309906a9. Summary will update on new commits.

+### 14.2 Two source-backed defects and the identity limit
+
+**Claude accepted successor can be overtaken by the preceding result.** In `claude-sdk/session.ts` blob `51b1e49aea3db62fbc991edba4c8e207edb65cab`, accepting B synchronously clears `lastSuccessfulInput` at lines 109–111. If A is still active, A's later successful terminal sets that slot back to A at 394–396 without checking the already accepted successor. The original next-input path awaits `checkReadiness` at 242 before handing B to the SDK. While that original await is pending, `active` is undefined and the ordinary after-result suggestion for A passes 311. This is a concrete legal ordering through the actual Query fixture and original readiness seam, not a timing measurement or an observed vendor incident. The three existing optional Claude tests cover an immediate duplicate, a foreign session, internal filtering, a late frame while the next input is active and default-off, but not this accepted-queue ordering.
+
+The same wire format also limits recovery after overtaking. Root read the installed exact SDK 0.3.305 declarations: `Options` documents at most one `prompt_suggestion` per turn, arriving after that turn's `result`, with suppression including the first turn, errors, plan mode and other settings/limits. `SDKPromptSuggestionMessage` has `type`, `suggestion`, `uuid` and `session_id`; it has no native turn/input ID and supplies no cross-turn completion-order guarantee. A first outstanding A suggestion delivered after B's terminal cannot be assigned to B merely because B most recently completed. A local counter, session ID, UUID or arrival order cannot manufacture the missing native lineage. The correction must cover both the queued-B case and this late-A-after-B case, without claiming an undocumented SDK ordering rule.
+
+**Codex local RPC expiry discards the only native cancellation handle.** In RPC blob `40fce90046397607a009f9b70e5b66421933cfeb`, 64–75 delete a sent pending request and reject `request-timeout` with unknown acceptance without aborting the caller signal. In app-server blob `924e2dc8b09fb90c081e47fc0b803079b50f85ae`, 155–158 then mark the sample settled and remove its only abort/cancel listener; driver blob `c77809d097940bed17cebc13b849f57f13a0db0b`, 257–258, clears `sampleAbort`. A later accepted ordinary input cannot cancel that original sample, and a later completed turn may launch another. The original finite subprocess fixture `8ac9c649390148b9930b7c7061f6f77fea6c5f8b` retains `pendingSamples` at 94 until exact `thread/sample/cancel` at 103–109; ordinary `turn/start` at 112 does not clear them. A valid short `rpcLimits.requestTimeoutMs` therefore exposes the defect using existing controlled transport only. The four new Codex tests exercise cancellation before the timeout, not this ordering. Local expiry is not native terminal or physical cleanup evidence.
+
+These two findings have independent source review; no real Claude/Codex process, model request, version command or new runtime experiment was used to establish them. They do not explain historical Windows readiness failures, change those outcomes, or establish that an original `confirmStopped` failed. The current optional feature remains default-off and is not being enabled in any product.
+
+### 14.3 Authorized producer policy: one original binding, bounded uncertainty
+
+**Claude — one captured Query, one pending auxiliary slot, one private quarantine.** Track only the exact already-owned original input that actually reaches this Query's existing handoff and its original terminal state. Do not derive identity from text, display role, UUID ordering, native session alone or a guessed SDK turn counter. A newly accepted successor that overtakes a prior potentially outstanding native suggestion makes subsequent auxiliary attribution uncertain. The same applies if an older queued input reaches its original handoff after a successor has already been admitted. Once that ambiguity is present, retain a private auxiliary quarantine for this captured Query's lifetime and suppress ambiguous offers. Normal inputs, queue admission, readiness, terminal events, interactions, checkpoints, interrupt, close and physical custody continue through their existing paths; quarantine must not seal, interrupt, restart or replace the native Query.
+
+The potential native auxiliary slot must also account for an internal/ineligible input: the SDK option is Query-scoped and can generate after internal work even though Host eligibility correctly suppresses display. A late internal candidate cannot borrow the next human input. Retire an unambiguous slot only from its own already-bound observation/lifecycle facts; consume a valid same-session after-result auxiliary frame at most once before calling the observer, even when its text is empty/invalid or the offer fails. Foreign/nested/restore frames cannot consume or establish another input's ownership. Recheck the captured slot, open state and quarantine after the existing eligibility callback, which may reenter ordinary admission/close; observer errors remain isolated and never become ordinary Session failure.
+
+A successful result is necessary for an offer but is not proof that no old suggestion can arrive. Interrupt, failure or absence of a suggestion cannot silently rebind uncertain old work to B. Once quarantine is set, a later candidate, ordinary success, callback return or cancel acknowledgment does not clear it. There is no proven same-Query recovery criterion in the documented wire, so no such criterion may be invented. State starts fresh only in an independently caller-created new Query through the already existing open path; this correction starts no Query. The SDK's documented first-turn suppression is not permission to invent a native counter: an unobserved prior suggestion can conservatively suppress later auxiliary output for that Query. This limitation must remain explicit; the change does not qualify complete native next-prompt availability. A flow where the original unambiguous A observation was consumed before B admission must still permit B's independently bound suggestion.
+
+**Codex — retain uncertain sent-sample ownership inside the existing client.** The existing `onSentId` reports original frame-dispatch admission, not provider acceptance. Capture that original ID once. If a potentially sent sample ends through local timeout/abort/other uncertain transport settlement without an observed native response, synchronously latch auxiliary sampling unavailable for that client lifetime before discarding the local listener/slot. Attempt at most one best-effort `thread/sample/cancel` for that captured ID while the original RPC transport is open, sharing one once-only flag between explicit abort and uncertain-error handling. Use the existing request queue and original RPC budgets; no new clock, deadline, retry, process, parent `turn/interrupt`, replay or second cancellation. Closed transport cannot be reopened to send it.
+
+Do not promote an uncertain sample after a cancel ACK: that acknowledges the control request, while late original RPC replies are already discarded by the original pending-map logic. Without a retained exact-original terminal proof, further auxiliary samples stay refused on this client; ordinary turns and readiness remain usable. Known-not-sent rejection, a received definite native error response (including unsupported method), and a received sample result are distinct from local unknown termination and must not be relabeled as physical cleanup failure. Preserve the original thrown error object and successful native response. Existing driver `close` and `confirmStopped` remain the only existing physical cleanup path; no sample flag, ACK, EOF or local rejection substitutes for that receipt. The conservative client-wide auxiliary latch is bounded state, not a new transport/session owner.

+1. Claude: run the actual original Query and Session; hand A once, synchronously admit B while A is active, hold only B's original readiness callback, settle A, and emit the ordinary A after-result suggestion before releasing that callback. Verify zero offers while both original inputs/handoffs/results and their identities remain valid. Baseline must fail the offered-candidate assertion, not fixture setup, an unavailable private helper, a missing marker or an artificial clock.
+2. Claude: finish A without consuming its auxiliary frame, admit and finish B, then emit A's first delayed same-session frame. Verify no B attribution and that later success cannot clear the auxiliary quarantine. Include the same ambiguity from an internal/ineligible prior input. A complementary actual Query flow must retain one correct candidate per input when each unambiguous prior frame is consumed before the next admission. Keep default-off, foreign/nested/invalid/duplicate suppression, close/interrupt boundaries, one Query and original input counts. Eligibility/offer callback errors or reentrant admission must not escape into normal lifecycle.
+3. Codex: use the actual finite subprocess/connected client, its exact completed native turn, existing `sample-mode: hold`, and an explicitly selected short valid original RPC timeout. Await the actual original request-timeout error to establish that local settlement; require exactly one cancellation carrying that sample's observed request ID. Baseline must fail missing targeted cancellation after that actual timeout. Do not substitute a sleeps-only assertion, mocked timeout implementation or copied sample method.
+4. Codex: after the same uncertain sent sample, an ordinary following turn must still start and complete with exact original thread/turn identity, but another auxiliary sample must be refused before an additional sample frame. Baseline must fail the expected refusal/extra-frame assertion. A cancel reply must not unlock the latch; an explicit abort racing the timeout must not duplicate cancellation. Known-not-sent/pre-aborted requests produce no native cancellation or unknown-work latch; a definite native unsupported response may be handled as none without disabling later separately valid auxiliary work. Preserve unchanged main `turn/start` counts, no parent interrupt/replay, normal response/error identity and original close/custody receipts.
+
+These are real controlled mechanisms through existing test seams. The synthetic fixture's pending map demonstrates protocol bookkeeping; it does not establish vendor or OS custody. name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ['24.21.0', '26.11.1']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Setup Node24 Corepack source
        uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6
        with:
          node-version: 24.21.0
          package-manager-cache: false
      - name: Setup selected Node
        uses: actions/setup-node@249970729cb0ef3589644e2896645e5dc5ba9c38 # v6
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          package-manager-cache: false
      - name: Select pinned pnpm through selected Node
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          selectedNode="$(node -p 'process.execPath')"
          corepackJs="$RUNNER_TOOL_CACHE/node/24.21.0/$(node -p 'process.arch')/lib/node_modules/corepack/dist/corepack.js"
          test -f "$corepackJs"
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/toolchain/bin" "$RUNNER_TEMP/toolchain/corepack"
          printf '#!/bin/sh\nexec "%s" "%s" pnpm@11.18.0 "$@"\n' "$selectedNode" "$corepackJs" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/toolchain/bin/pnpm"
          chmod 755 "$RUNNER_TEMP/toolchain/bin/pnpm"
          printf '%s\n' "$RUNNER_TEMP/toolchain/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          printf 'COREPACK_HOME=%s\n' "$RUNNER_TEMP/toolchain/corepack" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          COREPACK_HOME="$RUNNER_TEMP/toolchain/corepack" "$selectedNode" "$corepackJs" pnpm@11.18.0 --version
      - name: Install exact dependency graph
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts
      - name: Types, controlled tests and packed consumers
        env:
          # Retain the SAME exact bytes installed by the package-consumer test.
          AGENT_TEAMS_PROVIDER_PACK_TEST_RETAIN_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/checked-v2-spi
        run: pnpm check
      - name: Record exact-head checked archives (not a Host qualification)
        if: matrix.node == '24.21.0'
        shell: bash
        env:
          EXPECTED_HEAD: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
        run: |
          node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
          import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process'
          import { readFileSync, readdirSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs'
          import { join } from 'node:path'
          const root = join(process.env.RUNNER_TEMP, 'checked-v2-spi')
          const names = readdirSync(root).filter(name => name.endsWith('.tgz')).sort()
          if (names.length !== 2 ||
              names.filter(name => name.startsWith('agent-teams-provider-implementations-')).length !== 1 ||
              names.filter(name => name.startsWith('agent-teams-provider-session-contracts-')).length !== 1)
            throw Error('expected_exact_two_consumer_checked_archives')
          const head = execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', 'HEAD'], { encoding: 'utf8' }).trim()
          if (head !== process.env.EXPECTED_HEAD) throw Error('unexpected_checkout_head')
          const packages = names.map(name => {
            const data = readFileSync(join(root, name))
            return { file: name, bytes: data.length,
              sha256: createHash('sha256').update(data).digest('hex') }
          })
          const receipt = { schemaVersion: 1, sourceCommit: head, packages,
            qualification: 'source-and-packed-consumer-only',
            nativeHostQualified: false, packagedElectronQualified: false }
          writeFileSync(join(root, 'receipt.json'), JSON.stringify(receipt, null, 2) + String.fromCharCode(10))
          console.log(JSON.stringify(receipt))
          NODE
      - name: Upload TEST-only exact-HEAD checked provider and Session SPI archives
        if: matrix.node == '24.21.0'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
        with:
          name: opencode-v2-spi-consumer-checked-${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/checked-v2-spi/
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

          OPENCODE_V2_MCP_RECEIPT: ${{ github.workspace }}/native-v2-${{ matrix.proof }}-proof.json
          OPENCODE_V2_MCP_VERSION: ${{ matrix.proof == 'embedded-target-mcp' && '2.1.4' || '2.0.21' }}
          OPENCODE_V2_TEST_EXPECTED_PLATFORM: ${{ matrix.os == 'macos-15' && 'darwin-arm64' || matrix.os == 'macos-15-intel' && 'darwin-x64' || matrix.os == 'windows-2022' && 'win32-x64' || matrix.os == 'windows-11-arm' && 'win32-arm64' || 'linux-x64' }}
        run: node scripts/native-v2-mcp-proof.mjs

immediatePRs.body:
## Why
The existing frontend offers browser and device-code Codex login. The extracted app-server client currently exposes account reads/refresh/logout but cannot drive those login workflows through Host custody.

## Changes
Add finite typed account/login/start, account/login/cancel and private completion observation. Preserve native login IDs, unknown acceptance and no replay. The consumer keeps browser presentation, early-ID correlation, process custody, credential ownership and account readback. Session SPI and conversation event delivery remain compatible.

## Validation
Node 24.21.0 / pnpm 11.18.0: pnpm check passed (build, typecheck, 509 source tests and both packed consumers). The subprocess protocol suite covers 7 login cases. Node 26.11.1 / pnpm 11.18.0 also passed the complete check (509 source tests and both packed consumers). The retained packed-consumer artifact has SHA-256 `691a7a62cdd5a92e2edb120f2c409790c9ca16215495cdf9daa099b3b8748bd9`; the Session SPI archive is byte-identical to the frontend's current pin. This is protocol evidence, not vendor authentication or Desktop UI acceptance.

Frontend integration: https://github.com/777genius/agent-teams-ai/pull/1186
Plan: docs/plans/provider-migration/frontend-parity-2026-11-12/01-codex-login.md in that repository.

No package/release publication or default-branch merge.

immediatePRs.title: fix: fence stale Claude suggestions and uncertain Codex samples
immediatePRs.body: ## Problem Two opt-in prompt-suggestion paths can lose the identity or cancellation ownership of their original native work. Claude can restore A's suggestion slot after B was already accepted, and its wire event cannot identify a late A frame after B completes. Codex drops the sent sample's cancellation handle when its local RPC timeout expires, allowing later auxiliary work while the original sample remains unknown. ## Scope and current stage This isolated repair branch preserves all 43 commits and both Thinking changes through `9423f600dfb04d04448326dbced89919924b0b5f`. It does not move PR #8's shared head. The published R1 is §14 of `docs/plans/2026-11-14-native-next-prompt-suggestions.md`, commit `3ac086d1c157645faa358f0578f8dc764c950d66`. The current stage contains documentation only. Two additive finite-fixture test files come next. Both actual semantic REDs and independent source review are required before the bounded Claude Session and Codex app-server producer changes. The intended behavior is auxiliary-only lifetime quarantine for ambiguous Claude attribution and an unknown-sample latch plus at-most-once cancellation of Codex's original sent request. Ordinary inputs, readiness, queueing, deadlines, interactions and physical cleanup remain under their existing contracts. Suggestions remain default-off. ## Validation and boundaries Use the unchanged original `pnpm check` CI on Node 24.21.0 and 26.11.1 with pnpm 11.18.0, including both packed consumers. Earlier 9423 results—540 controlled passes and its checked archive pair—remain historical evidence and do not qualify the repair. Retain exact-head RED/GREEN logs and the newly checked archive pair before any separate atomic consumer adoption. Keep this PR Draft. The four original workflows were reviewed: safe CI is reachable; the Codex native job is Draft-skipped; Claude native and native OpenCode V2 paths do not match this bounded repair. No real Claude/Codex executable, SDK process, model request or version command; no manual dispatch, rerun, cancellation, native qualification or deadline extension. Product composer work and application archive/SPI adoption are outside this PR. --- ## Summary by cubic Fences stale Claude suggestions and uncertain Codex samples in the optional prompt-suggestion paths. Claude accepted-queue ordering can let a delayed earlier suggestion restore its slot after a successor was admitted, and the wire event has no input ID to disambiguate it. Codex local RPC expiry discards the only cancellation handle for a potentially sent sample, leaving unknown auxiliary work. - Claude: tracks the original suggestion owner; successor admission, interrupt, or uncertainty latches auxiliary offers off for the Query's lifetime, with no invented recovery criterion. - Codex: retains the sent sample's ID, latches auxiliary sampling on uncertain settlement, and attempts at most one targeted `thread/sample/cancel` while the transport is open. - Adds regression fixtures to `claude-sdk.test.ts` and `codex-subprocess.test.ts` plus the R1 plan documenting the defects and edit boundary. Suggestions remain default-off; no real Claude/Codex process is invoked. Written for commit c79b81bf002eaac95436da71c7049d7f309906a9. Summary will update on new commits.
